rookie_wall_dependence_on_production.classification_evidence: Week-blocked 95% CI [-3.4263, +0.6508] crosses zero -- the expected shape for a real small signal at this window size, not a resolved wrong sign (wrong_sign_resolved requires the WHOLE interval below zero). no_split_half_reliability is inadmissible: the underlying dependence metric's own reliability was already measured and recorded separately (rookie_wall_dependence_reliability, r=0.988 within-season / 0.129 season-to-season, both entirely positive), so the trait is not unreliable in the sense that ground requires. Positive control (candidate replaced by realized ats_margin) reads +44.298 accuracy points, week-blocked P+ 1.0 -- the harness is proven sensitive to an effect of that size before this screen result is read.
rookie_wall_dependence_on_production.description: LEAD-24 stage 2: rookie_wall_dependence_fade_flag stacked on production weak_stack, opener-graded, rotation window [2020,2021]. Signed +1 when the AWAY team's trailing top-50-pick-rookie snap-share dependence is in the season-week's top quintile AND week>=12 (favour home, predeclared FADE direction), -1 when the HOME team's is, 0 otherwise/both. Reuses LEAD-24 Stage 1's already-reliable dependence metric (docs/rookie_wall.md, reliability recorded separately as rookie_wall_dependence_reliability).
rookie_wall_dependence_on_production.plain_summary: Fading the team leaning hardest on high-draft-pick rookies late in the season, stacked on top of the production model, read slightly negative (-1.3 accuracy points) on a two-season opener test -- the interval still crosses zero, so this is not a settled result either way.
